overview.goal: Build a Wallboard-connected application for an end customer or partner, as a standalone site or a CMS My Apps integration using a hosted URL or uploaded HTML bundle.
audience: End customers building applications for themselves
overview.source: Public integration code, optional Vue components, standalone TypeScript/Vue examples, a portable embedded HTML/ZIP example, and a Node/SQLite example.
overview.runtime: Standalone users sign in through the application's Wallboard OAuth flow. CMS users approve registered method/path permissions before an embedded app loads. The CMS performs allowed API requests over a private MessagePort; the iframe never receives a Wallboard access or refresh token. Normal backend API permissions, the approved declaration and effective read-only mode all apply.
overview.capabilityBoundary: MCP supplies authoring guidance and existing authenticated tools for API work and Custom UI registration. The builder owns source, preview, artifacts and any external hosting/backend. CMS integration requires the matching deployed Custom UI feature; uploadable signage widget packages remain a separate surface using custom_app_guide.

workflow: Resolve purpose, actors, read/write operations, customer scope, visual identity, target device/surface, application-owned records and hosting/source ownership.

Resolve delivery: standalone site, CMS hosted HTTPS URL, or CMS uploaded HTML bundle. For CMS delivery, resolve the app name, selected numeric customer, customer/platform ownership and authorized audience before registration. Declare every actual API method/path and whether the app is permanently read-only.

For externally hosted delivery or an application backend, resolve delivery.hostingChoice before provider-specific setup or deployment. A CMS static bundle uses Wallboard hosting and does not require another frontend hosting provider. Continue portable implementation and local validation while an unanswered hosting question is pending.

Select the kit checkout using the MCP response's starterSource: new projects use current main unless the user selects a revision; preserve existing project pins and record the actual checkout SHA. guideProvenance identifies the canonical guide, not the required starter revision.
Read AGENTS.md, README.md and the relevant docs; run npm ci and npm run check.
Call get_current_user before authorized customer API work. Use api_howto for verified operations and get_branding for authorized branding; retain normal permissions.
Choose a browser-only app for direct Wallboard operations, or add a backend/database for application-owned workflow state, jobs or server-side credentials.

For standalone delivery, use npm run build then npm run new-app -- <vue|vanilla> <new-directory>. For CMS delivery, adapt examples/embedded-device-board or an existing frontend with createEmbeddedWallboardClient. The standalone generator has no embedded option; no published npm package is required.
Reuse connection code and platform components; adapt presentation to the application's brand and workflow. Other frameworks can use the same browser core or OAuth/REST contract.
Validate using synthetic fixtures and inspect the actual UI. Perform live writes only when explicitly authorized against designated test records.

For CMS delivery, call api_howto with categories:["customui"] and follow delivery.cmsRegistration using ordinary api_write and api_proxy_url. Preserve the app ID on updates and verify the requested customer's availability.

Deploy hosted components through the chosen provider's actual process. Prove the selected standalone OAuth or CMS embedded flow, provider/runtime/storage requirements and actual UI before claiming deployment or embedding works.

authentication.browser: createWallboardClient handles standalone OAuth discovery, optional public-client registration, PKCE, one-use callback state, tab-local sessions, single-flight rotating refresh and a verified /api/v2/user/me profile. createEmbeddedWallboardClient uses protocol 2 with a compatible CMS MessagePort host: verified identity/context and API requests/results, without tokens, direct Wallboard fetch, OAuth or storage in the iframe.
authentication.configuration: Standalone apps use a configured public clientId when DCR is unavailable and register the exact callback URI; default callbacks use the origin. CMS embedded apps use the host bootstrap and need no separate OAuth client or callback.
authentication.session: Use one client per application/server. Standalone sessionStorage is tab-local and shared storage requires coordinated refresh. Embedded getToken rejects API_PROXY_ONLY; host credentials never cross into the app. Calls support cancellation and a bounded timeout, with no uncertain write replay. Never put tokens in URLs, logs, application records or source, including the builder MCP token.
authentication.authority: Authenticated API responses establish standalone identity; the trusted CMS host supplies the same verified identity for embedded clients. Decoded standalone JWT display hints never establish authorization. Embedded profile fields forwarded by the iframe cannot authenticate an application backend.
authentication.backend: Standalone OAuth applications can use createWallboardValidator with a configured trusted server; its online /me validation follows no redirects and caches no identity by default. Embedded app backends, jobs and databases need a separate explicit authentication design because the iframe has no host Wallboard JWT.
authentication.localVerification: JWKS-only validation needs a verified signing-key format and explicit issuer/audience/key refresh/revocation policy. Check the deployed version; resource audience behavior must be verified rather than inferred.

api.contractSource: Use the existing api_howto, target /v3/api-docs and public API reference for endpoint/body contracts. Typed kit helpers are selected fields, not a second complete schema.
api.helpers: Direct standalone or tokenless embedded transport, explicit forCustomer(customerId), WB/FIELDS/entity subsets, WBQL, pagination, datasource and media helpers. Embedded requests are JSON-only and have no app-supplied headers, binary streaming or file-upload transport; raw reconstructs status/body/content type.
api.tenantScope: Generic tenant requests need an explicit customerId; instance:true is a deliberate server-wide operation. Global admins select a customer before tenant queries.
api.permissions: Wallboard enforces role, customer, team and read-only restrictions. The embedded host additionally requires approved method/path declarations and enforces account OR host-forced OR app-declared read-only mode. Host-owned auth/elevation routes are unavailable and no temporary elevated CMS credential is silently reused. Preserve 403 outcomes; do not search for a bypass.
api.writes: Verify the actual write contract, replacement/cascade behavior and requested user intent. No automatic retry of uncertain network writes.
api.ui: Use loading/empty/error/forbidden states and discard superseded customer/filter requests. Branding is an explicit application input.

backend.example: examples/node-notes provides Node HTTP and parameterized SQLite CRUD scoped to configured server, customer and user.
backend.authorization: resolveCustomerScope requires global admins to explicitly choose an application-allowlisted customer, even when their verified profile contains a customerId. Regular users may use their own customer. The example write policy is disabled by default.
backend.storage: The app owns its database schema, retention and access rules. Use a durable database supported by the provider; an ephemeral SQLite file is not production persistence.
backend.sessionBoundary: The shipped backend accepts standalone OAuth bearer tokens per request. Embedded apps cannot forward a host token and need separate backend authentication. A cookie-session BFF requires a complete callback, secure session, CSRF and logout implementation.
backend.adaptation: Other backend languages or provider runtimes can implement the same validated /me identity and application data boundary; Node is an executable reference.

embedding.standalone: For standalone apps, prove top-level OAuth and hosting. CMS embedded apps instead prove permission approval, host launch, private MessagePort, verified profile, tokenless API results and cancellation/cleanup; do not add an iframe OAuth flow.
embedding.frameRequirements: Verify response frame policy, the specific Wallboard surface's sandbox, browser storage and interactive input. CMS and signage frames have different capabilities.
embedding.login: Standalone signIn rejects framed login and requires top-level navigation. CMS My Apps uses createEmbeddedWallboardClient protocol 2; deploy the matching CMS feature and rebuild older embedded apps. The host supplies verified identity/context and performs only approved requests without passing any Wallboard token to the iframe. There is no version 1 token fallback. Approved operations still use the actual user normal resource authority; selected customer is a request default. Closing/removing an app stops new proxy operations and aborts pending calls but cannot undo completed writes.
embedding.executionPolicy: In v1 CUSTOMER-owned apps, whether hosted URLs or HTML bundles, require an actual authenticated non-ADMIN account belonging to the app's immutable owning customer. The backend compares the CMS signed JWT's own customerId with the stored owner; selected customer and network membership do not grant runtime access. ADMIN and reseller/network OWNER visiting a member customer's app receive 403. A reseller OWNER may launch apps owned by its own customer with its normal API authority. Metadata management keeps its existing permissions. Customer selection, confirming trust and frontend View As/impersonation do not change the account's customer or narrow its underlying API authority. PLATFORM apps retain the current user's normal resource authority subject to approved operations and mode, including explicitly trusted ADMIN launches; do not automatically copy/re-register a refused customer app as a platform workaround.
embedding.customerPreview: A real backend customer-preview/delegation session is a separate step 2 and is not available in v1. Frontend View As changes presentation, not the execution token.
embedding.productBoundary: The deployed Custom UI feature supports named My Apps entries from hosted HTTPS URLs or uploaded HTML bundles. Customer-owned apps remain private to that customer; ADMIN platform apps may be assigned to selected customers or explicitly published to all. This is separate from display CustomApp/widget packaging and permissions.
embedding.isolation: CMS runs an opaque sandbox with allow-scripts and no allow-same-origin. Do not add storage, cookie-session, popup or sandbox exceptions to make a provider work. Null origin is not provider identity. Uploaded documents also require the resource server's enforced CSP sandbox; verify asset/API CORS and relative paths. See docs/hosting.md and the portable embedded example.
embedding.evidence: An API registration, header check or successful build does not prove the actual CMS iframe flow. Verify the matching deployed frontend/backend/storage/proxy and the chosen provider separately.

permissions.registration: Store apiPermissions:[{method,path,description?}] and readOnly:boolean with app metadata for both hosted URLs and HTML bundles. Each GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE method is separate. Maximum 128 declarations; path maximum 2048 characters and optional description maximum 500. A canonical /api/ path has a literal resource segment and subsequent [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ literals or complete {identifier} placeholders. No duplicates, globs, regex, external origins, encoded aliases, query or fragment.
permissions.approval: The CMS displays the complete method/path list and optional author descriptions before loading the iframe. No proxy calls run until approval. Changed declaration/source requires renewed approval; the iframe cannot grant itself access. Permissions authorize endpoint shapes, not separate resource ownership or tenant scope.
permissions.readOnly: Any account read-only flag, host-forced mode or app-declared readOnly locks the launch to read-only. A declared read-only app cannot switch to write mode. GET is allowed except known mutating/authentication routes; exact POST exceptions /api/deviceStat/{deviceId}/graphs and /api/v2/device/requestLog still need declaration and approval. Explain that diagnostic-log collection triggers device activity. The CMS independently checks every request.
permissions.manifest: The embedded example includes informational wallboard-ui.json containing apiPermissions and readOnly for registration/import. Registered metadata is authoritative; merely uploading the file does not grant permissions. This is not a signage CustomApp manifest.

hostingChoice.defaultSuggestion: On an OpenAI platform with Sites actually available and compatible with the application's requirements, offer Sites as the default hosting option. Explain that it can provide a hosted application and usable URL without arranging a separate deployment workflow.
hostingChoice.userChoice: Ask the user to choose or confirm hosting before provider-specific provisioning or deployment, unless they have already explicitly chosen or authorized it. For example: Would you like me to publish this with Sites and give you a hosted link, use another provider, or keep it local? An unanswered question is not approval. Make source, preview where available and validation outcomes reviewable before requesting publishing approval. Respect an existing authorization and do not repeat an answered question.
hostingChoice.existingInstructions: An explicit provider, repository, runtime, deployment pipeline, audience or local-only instruction takes precedence over the default suggestion. Keep those constraints; do not silently change providers, move source, replace the database or expand sharing.
hostingChoice.compatibility: Check actual Sites capability and the selected provider's callback, runtime and durable-storage requirements. If Sites is unavailable or incompatible, explain the concrete limitation and offer a compatible provider or editable-source handoff. The Node/SQLite reference is not automatically compatible with a serverless runtime. A hosting choice alone does not authorize replacing an explicitly chosen runtime or database: explain the necessary adaptation and get the user's choice before changing those constraints.

cmsRegistration.availability: Confirm the target server has the Custom UI API and matching CMS frontend, storage and proxy isolation deployed. Unsupported endpoints or an unavailable CMS surface remain a deployment gate; deliver source/artifacts and report the gate rather than claiming registration or runtime success.
cmsRegistration.contract: Use api_howto with categories:["customui"] and the target API schema for exact paths, DTOs, defaults and errors. Keep endpoint documentation there; do not invent CustomApp manifests or another endpoint catalogue.
cmsRegistration.scope: Customer-owned collection/create calls require OWNER+ and the selected numeric customerId. Private ID-addressed detail/update/delete/upload calls derive and authorize the stored customer owner and require no customerId query. Availability/launch keep the selected runtime customer. ADMIN may instead create a platform app using MCP customerId:-1 for that explicit global operation. Platform assignment IDs still identify real selected customers; do not use -1 as a tenant or assignment ID.
cmsRegistration.publication: Preserve the user's authorized ownership and audience. Platform availableToAllCustomers defaults to false; assign only the selected customers, or set it true only for an explicitly chosen global audience. Customer-owned apps have no assignment/publication fields. Normal role and read-only refusals remain authoritative.
cmsRegistration.metadata: Use ordinary api_write to create or update HOSTED_URL or HTML_BUNDLE metadata and separate platform assignments. Read back existing metadata before updates, retain its app ID and immutable ownership/source kind, and preserve fields outside the requested change. A hosted URL must already serve the compatible app; registration does not deploy that host or its backend. Include verified apiPermissions declarations and readOnly. The example wallboard-ui.json is an import/source aid, not automatic backend ZIP parsing or an authority grant.
cmsRegistration.upload: For HTML_BUNDLE, build a ZIP with regular index.html at its root and relative assets; it remains unready until upload succeeds. Request api_proxy_url for the exact ID-addressed POST upload path from api_howto; customer-owned uploads authorize the stored owner and need no customerId query. From the execution environment send multipart field file with MIME application/zip. Treat the short-lived authenticated proxy URL as a credential; keep it out of frontend source, logs and public handoffs. Renew the URL only for the proxy's explicit invalid/expired-token error; preserve upstream permission failures. After an uncertain upload failure, read back metadata/revision and resolve the outcome before any retry; do not automatically repeat writes. The existing file_upload/api_upload_from_url tools target media files and are not this bundle upload flow.
cmsRegistration.verification: Read back metadata and the selected customer's available catalogue, then verify the named My Apps entry and actual launch as an intended runtime user. CUSTOMER apps require the runtime account to belong to the immutable owning customer; an ADMIN or visiting reseller account can manage metadata but cannot be used as runtime proof. PLATFORM apps keep normal user authority. Preserve role/tenant/403/404 outcomes; successful metadata or upload calls alone do not prove CMS permission approval, rendering, tokenless API execution or provider compatibility.
cmsRegistration.handoff: Report the stable app ID, name, source kind, ownership, selected customer and publication audience, source/ZIP or actual hosted URL, and which deployment/runtime checks passed or remain unverified.

required: Editable source and exact kit revision
Validation results and explicit unverified runtime behavior
CMS app ID, ownership, selected customer and publication audience when registered
delivery.publishing: Deploy through the user's confirmed provider with authorized ownership and audience. Git source publication, npm package publication and deployed hosting are separate outcomes.
delivery.sourcePrivacy: Use synthetic fixtures. Never include runtime tokens, the builder's MCP credentials, private customer application source or private server registries.

checklist: SDK and generated project type-check and build; meaningful auth/customer/database tests pass.
Inspect signed-out, loading, empty, error, long-name and mobile UI states.

For standalone delivery, prove OAuth callback, refresh, logout policy and rejected/expired credentials on the deployed origin. For CMS delivery, prove the private port, verified host profile, no token/direct-fetch fallback, parallel replies, cancellation/timeouts and host cleanup.

Prove customer scope, forbidden behavior and any application database isolation. For CMS CUSTOMER apps, prove the owning-account match, ADMIN/visiting-reseller refusal and same-customer reseller allowance; PLATFORM apps retain ordinary user authority.
Confirm consequential writes against verified contracts and designated test records.
Prove provider routing, runtime and durable storage assumptions; a ZIP frontend does not supply an application backend or database.

For CMS delivery, verify app metadata/availability, authorized audience, source replacement and disabled/unassigned/customer/logout lifecycle on the actual host. Report embedding as verified only after that flow passes.

For CMS delivery, approve the displayed declaration before launch; prove denied undeclared methods/paths, read-only write refusal and exact POST exceptions, changed-source/declaration approval invalidation and an app-declared read-only lock.

finalAnswerContract: Return editable source location, exact kit revision, what was built, startup/build/configuration steps, validation outcomes and actual preview/deployment URL or ZIP artifact. For CMS registration include the stable app ID, selected customer, ownership and authorized audience. Clearly identify deployment availability, live login, provider/database durability and iframe behaviors that remain unverified. Never include authenticated proxy URLs or tokens.
